raw_nl: The controller shall check the communication of the controller with the sensors and valves.
If the SelfTest fails, the controller shall not be able to proceed to ventilation.
The controller shall check the communication of the controller with GUI.
The breath cycle shall start with the inspiration phase.
The controller shall implement the following modes (see Figure 4.1):
At the end of an inspiration phase, if the Inspiratory Pause is set by the GUI, an Inspiratory Pause shall start (see CONT.41).
When the ventilator is in Start-up or VentilationOff mode, the in valve pressure shall be set to close and the out valve shall be open.
In PCV and PSV modes there shall be the possibility to initiate an Inspiratory Pause if it is set by the GUI.
The inspiration phase lasts until the inspiration peak is reached but no later than the max_insp_time_psv is over. After that the expiration phase begins.
A set of default values for all parameters shall be provided and loaded from a configuration file on the machine when it is turned on. The parameters are listed in Section 3.1.1.
Before monitoring a sudden drop in pressure above the inhale trigger sensitivity ITS, the controller shall wait for the trigger window (0.7 sec).
The transition from Start-up Mode to Self test Mode shall occur once the configurations have been loaded and the internal checking is terminated.
The controller cannot return from fail-safe mode to any other mode without a power cycle (turn off and then turn on the machine).
The Recruitment Maneuver, if not actively stopped by the GUI, has a timeout (max_rm_time). After the Recruitment Maneuver phase expiration phase begins.
Fail-safe: the controller forces input and output valves to their de-energized states (in valve close and out valve open)
In PCV and PSV modes there shall be the possibility to initiate an Expiratory Pause if it is set by the GUI.
The transition from VentilationOff to PSV shall occur if the change mode command is received from the GUI.
If the patient is in expiration phase:

In PCV and PSV mode, at the end of an inspiration and if inspiratory pause is not required, it shall be possible to initiate a lung recruitment procedure, termed Recruitment Maneuver (RM), if it is required by the GUI. Not available in North America.
The transition from PSV to VentilationOff shall occur if the user stops the ventilation in PSV mode.

When the Expiratory Pause is set by the GUI, the ventilator shall wait for the end of the next expiration phase, and if the Expiratory Pause is still required, both the inspiratory and expiratory valves will close until the expiratory pause is stopped by the GUI.
The transition from VentilationOff to PCV mode shall occur if the change mode command is received from the GUI.
In RM the out valve shall be closed and the in valve shall be opened to allow lung inflation at PRM

When the Inspiratory Pause is set by the GUI, the ventilator shall wait for the end of the next inspiration phase, and if the Inspiratory Pause still required, both the inspiratory and expiratory valves will close until the inspiratory pause is stopped by the GUI.
During the self test mode the controller shall perform the self-test specified in the FUN.6.
In PSV mode the expiration phase shall start when the inspiratory flow drops below a setable fraction of the peak flow (Expiratory Trigger Setting)
The system shall log user-set ventilation and alarm parameters as well as the current calibration parameters.
The high-level operation sequence shall follow the scheme shown in Figure 2.1
When a PCV-to-PSV switch is initiated by the user the system shall ask the user for confirmation/setting of PSV parameters to be used
The system shall raise an alarm when a parameter value goes outside the range defined for its associated alarm.

Upon initiation of the Start-up Mode, the system shall go through an initialization process that loads default parameters and checks the system memory and the communication of the controller with the sensors and valves, as well as between the controller and the GUI.
A failure of the GUI (e.g. GUI freezes) or a loss of communication between the GUI and the Controller shall raise a high-priority alarm and any ongoing ventilation process shall not be interrupted.
Once the self-test has been completed successfully and configurations have been loaded properly the system shall start monitoring and reporting health parameters.
If “Resume Ventilation” is selected, every step of the self-test procedure FUN.6 can be skipped or optionally rerun individually.
In PSV mode the system shall check for the presence of apnea, which occurs when a patient does not take new breath within the allowable apnea lag time.
The system shall have a leak compensation feature for leaks in the patient breathing circuit which shall be disabled by default.
The patient shall not be connected to the breathing circuit when the system is powered on and through start-up and self-test.
The system shall prompt the user before ventilation is started to enter user-controlled alarm thresholds for SAV.3- SAV.9
In PCV mode, a new breathing cycle shall be initiated either after a breathing cycle is over, or by patient request during expiration.
If apnea is detected, an apnea alarm shall be triggered.
Once all self-test steps have been completed successfully, it shall be possible to proceed to the Standby Mode.
Once the start-up has been completed successfully the user must select “New Patient” or “Resume Ventilation” before the system transitions to self-test mode
The switch to PSV shall occur only after the PSV parameters have been confirmed and until that has happened the PCV ventilation shall continue

In Standby Mode ventilation shall be off and it shall be possible to adjust all user-controlled parameters for ventilation and alarms before connecting to the patient and starting patient ventilation.

The system shall indicate to the user that the initialization process has been completed successfully or failed. In case of a failure the user shall be warned that the system is out-of-service. In addition, any other operations shall be not allowed.
The switch to PSV shall occur at the end of a PCV inspiratory time
The system shall connect to pressurized gas supply of oxygen and medical air and accept pressures up to 5.2 bar.
The self-test procedure shall confirm the local alarms are functional.
Any failure of the gas supply shall leave the system in a state that allows the patient to inhale and exhale unimpeded.
The user shall be able to disable/enable the leak compensation feature at any time.
Once the power of the system has been off for more than 15 minutes it shall not be possible to select “Resume Ventilation”
The system shall log key parameters, save them before being powered off and load them upon start-up to be made available on a log page on the GUI.
A patient breath trigger shall reset the timer for the time-cycled breathing cycle.
The self-test procedure shall confirm the switchover from external to internal power works.
In PCV mode it shall be possible to initiate with the push of a single button a lung recruitment procedure, termed Recruitment Maneuver (RM). Note: This maneuver is not allowed in North America.
When enabled, the leak compensation shall be activated by the MinPEEP alarm (SAV.15)

The Start-up Mode shall be initiated by pushing the power button of the system once the system has been connected to the breathing circuit (without connection to the patient), the air supply, and the power source.
If the self-test fails, the user shall be warned that the system is out-of-service. In addition, any other operations shall be not allowed.
The self-test procedure shall confirm there are no unacceptable leaks in the breathing circuit.
If “New Patient” is selected, the user shall have to enter patient attributes and the completion of every step of the self-test procedure (FUN.6) shall be mandatory
The system shall provide means to switch from PCV to PSV while PCV ventilation is active.
The system shall provide a log to include the overall duration of the active use of the O2 sensor (%-hours)
If “Resume Ventilation” is selected, the system shall load the last calibration parameters, alarm thresholds, and ventilation parameters from the last active patient ventilation.
If the pressure sensor fails to connect or reports an error condition after a fixed number of retries (maximum 5), the controller shall transition to the fail-safe mode.
When expiratory pause timeout (max exp pause) is over, the cycle shall proceed immediately to inspiration.
VentilationOff: In ventilation off, the machine does not ventilate, the in valve is closed and the out valve is opened.

The transition from PSV to PCV shall occur if the patient does not trigger a breath within the time of the apnea trigger window. The switch shall occur with respiratory rate, target inspiratory pressure and I:E defined for the apnea backup mode.

Start-up Mode: In start-up mode the controller initializes itself with default configuration parameters (if any), checks the system memory and the communication of the controller with the sensors and valves, as well as between the controller and the GUI. Start-up mode is completed once the required activities have been completed.
The controller shall stop RM if it is required from the GUI.
When the ventilator is in an expiration state the in valve shall be closed (pressure 0) and the out valve shall be open.
The transition to Start-up Mode shall be allowed by pushing the power button located on the back side of the ventilator unit to turn it on
When inspiratory pause timeout (max_ins_pause) is over, the cycle shall proceed immediately to expiration.
min_exp_time_psv shall be the half of the last inspiration time. min_exp_time_psv shall be in the interval [0.4 : 2] sec.
If the external ADC fails to initialize or reports an error condition after a fixed number of retries (maximum 5), the controller shall transition to the fail-safe mode.

A new inspiration shall be initiated by a sudden drop in pressure above the inhale trigger sensitivity (ITS_PSV ), which shall be set by the user (i.e., it yields the condition drop(PAW) > ITS_PSV )).

The transition from PCV to PSV shall occur if ventilation is on, the transition from PCV to PSV shall occur at the end of a PCV inspiratory time if the change mode command has been received from the GUI.
The transition from PCV to VentilationOff shall occur if the user stops the ventilation in PCV mode.
Final State shall be reached by pushing the power button located on the back side of the ventilator unit to turn it off.
During Final state, all parameters (if any) are to be safely stored before the final state is complete and the unit is de-energized.
